name: Business Owner / Investor Residence Permit

requirements.blocker_text: There is no dedicated 'investor visa' in Bosnia and Herzegovina -- foreign nationals obtain residence by registering a company and then securing a work permit through it, following the same sequencing as employer-sponsored work (D Visa before entry, then a work permit, then temporary residence). Minimum share capital to form a limited liability company differs by entity: approximately 1,000 BAM (~EUR 511) in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, versus a symbolic 1 BAM in Republika Srpska. Registration runs through five stages -- name reservation at the Commercial Court Register, notarized incorporation documents with capital deposited into a temporary account, court registration at the competent cantonal court (5-15 days), registration with tax administration/statistics/health and pension funds, and account activation plus a municipal business license -- typically 20-45 days end to end. All foundation documents and personal records must be notarized and translated into Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian by a sworn translator.
requirements.fix_path: Register a limited liability company (minimum capital depends on entity: ~1,000 BAM in the Federation, ~1 BAM in Republika Srpska), complete the 5-stage registration process, then obtain a D Visa, work permit, and temporary residence through the company.

evidence_required.document: Power of attorney (if using local representation)
Proof of minimum share capital deposited

sources.title: Sonsoz Partner (law firm) -- company registration steps, minimum capital by entity, D Visa/work permit/residence sequencing for foreign investors

GENUINE FINDING: Bosnia has no standalone 'investor visa' category -- residence via business ownership runs entirely through the same company-registration-then-work-permit pipeline as ordinary employer sponsorship (see ba_work_permit.json), just with the applicant as their own sponsor. The capital threshold split between the Federation (~1,000 BAM) and Republika Srpska (~1 BAM symbolic) reflects Bosnia's two-entity legal structure, a recurring theme across this country's files. pr_after_months/citizenship_after_months mirror the general residence-based tracks (see ba_citizenship_naturalisation.json) and are NOT independently confirmed as applying automatically from this specific permit. family_can_work left null: not addressed by the source reviewed.
